channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Gerhard Schröder visits latest Russian employer, Hyperglobus
item.description: Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder visited a Moscow supermarket in his new role on the supervisory board. Schröder is no stranger to retirement stipends in Russia — or the scandal that accompanies them.

item.title: [DW] EU enlargement: European Commission tables reforms to prepare bloc for new members
item.description: The European Commission is proposing earlier access to EU markets for candidate countries, new voting rules to reduce vetoes and extra safeguards for a bigger bloc. But is the reform fair — or even feasible?

item.title: [DW] EU pulls sponsorship from Disinfo2026 event in Lithuania
item.description: The EU's diplomatic service, Canada and host nation Lithuania all pulled support from a disinformation event in Vilnius. Amid reports of US pressure, the EU said it was "uncomfortable with the framing" of some panels.

item.title: [DW] Security in the Black Sea region: is Bulgaria the weak link in Europe's defense against threats from Russia?
item.description: Two ships have sunk off the coast of Bulgaria and Romania after drone attacks in recent days. Bulgaria has held back on pointing the finger at Russia. What does that mean for security in the Black Sea and the region?

item.title: [DW] South Korea recalls Ukraine ambassador amid POW dispute
item.description: South Korea has said it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine. Seoul is upset about a transfer of North Korean prisoners of war being made public knowledge at the UN and had demanded — but not received — an apology.

item.title: [DW] As Russia steps up attacks on Ukrainian data centers, could Ukraine soon be offline?
item.description: As Russia targets Ukraine's data centers more and more, experts say the country's internet system is too robust to shut down entirely. However, services could become more expensive.

item.title: [DW] Middle Corridor: Can Bulgaria be a safe gateway for Asian imports to the EU?
item.description: The EU wants more trade via the Middle Corridor, which could bring big benefits for Bulgaria. But Tuesday's drone attacks on commercial ships off the Bulgarian coast are a stark reminder of the security risks involved.

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump faces Republican opposition to his diesel deal with Russia’s Putin
item.description: Lawmakers from both parties say the agreement would finance Putin’s war machine in Ukraine and violate US law

item.title: [DW] Who are the Ukrainian 'volunteers' under Russian command?
item.description: Russia has announced a battalion consisting of Ukrainian "volunteers." But veterans and former prisoners of war share very different accounts.

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs warn Irish EU budget plan is ‘short‑sighted’ and risks ‘historic failure’ as cuts of €141bn spare farm and cohesion funds
item.description: MEPs have instantly rejected a budget proposal by the Irish government, setting the scene for an institutional battle over the 2028-34 EU spending plan.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU leaders to speak no evil of Israel, as Nobel prize recalls Gaza ‘genocide’
item.description: EU leaders will stay mute on Gaza and merely "condemn" West Bank violence at next week's summit, as the 2026 Nobel peace prize highlights UN findings on Israel's "genocide".

item.title: [DW] Trump claims Russia and Ukraine agreed to 'energy ceasefire'
item.description: US President Donald Trump says both sides have agreed to stop targeting oil refineries, power plants and other energy infrastructure immediately.

item.title: [Financial Times] Not just ‘guys in flip-flops’: Houthis show reach with deadly strikes on Riyadh
item.description: Yemen’s Iran-backed militants have evolved from insurgency into potent armed force

item.title: [EU Observer] EU should use Digital Services Act against online tormentors of Belarusian and Russian exiles in Europe
item.description: By treating digital attacks on Belarusian and Russian exiles as a systemic risk under the DSA, the EU could reshape how global platforms handle online transnational repression.

item.title: [DW] Surrogacy in Georgia is booming but at what cost?
item.description: Georgia became a hub for surrogate pregnancies after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. DW spoke with parents, and those who wanted to become parents, about the hidden costs of a booming industry.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] France school protests go deeper than rioting or reactionism, says Sciences Po lecturer
item.description: Professor Jan Rovný argues French school protests could turn into a movment against spending cuts by a government with growing debt. He explains why private school pupils have joined publicly educated peers revolting on the streets, and how police violence will shape public mood.

item.title: [EU Observer] Who really owns Czech Vanadium? Investigators trace possible sanctions-evasion links to Russian oligarch Abramovich
item.description: Vanadium businesses owned by UAE-based entity appear to be linked with Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich. This has prompted complaints to police about the circumventing of sanctions.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Ukraine’s FM: Russia’s war budget makes the case for using frozen assets now
item.description: The aggressor has put a number on its intentions. Europe should turn Moscow’s reserves into Kyiv’s defense — collectively, lawfully and now.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Trump’s NATO envoy calls for moving military forces east as US reviews troops in Europe
item.description: Matthew Whitaker called for an overhaul of NATO’s bases and military infrastructure to move forces eastward as America reviews its troop presence in Europe.

item.title: [Financial Times] Diesel prices slip after Trump claims ‘energy ceasefire’ in Ukraine war
item.description: Announcement follows deal with Putin as US president tries to contain impact of higher fuel costs ahead of midterm elections

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Made in Europe’ wind, solar, and nuclear power can protect us from future energy shocks
item.description: Brussels is betting on a rapid build-out of homegrown renewables and nuclear to shield households and industry from the next energy shock.

item.title: [Politico Europe] UK’s Burnham says rejecting closer EU ties a ‘dereliction of duty’
item.description: The British prime minister will make the case for a closer relationship with the EU in a House of Commons statement Monday.

item.title: [Politico Europe] ‘This deal doesn’t help’: Europe slams Trump’s plan to buy Russian diesel
item.description: "Pressure, pressure, pressure on Russia" is the only way to end the war, Lithuania's foreign minister said.

item.title: [Financial Times] Putin is breaching Trump’s ‘energy ceasefire’, Zelenskyy says
item.description: Ukrainian president says Russia conducted strikes on power plants after US president’s announcement on Sunday

item.title: [Financial Times] Nobel Prize for economics awarded to Hall and Woodford
item.description: Live coverage of exciting economicsy stuff

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Should we be worried about Europe’s level of gas reserves?
item.description: European gas storage levels are unusually low for this time of year, reaching their lowest autumn level since 2011. With Russian gas imports set to end in 2027, could Europe face a tougher challenge in the months ahead?

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Ex-Bosnia envoy sees no risk of renewed violence, but the fractured country’s EU dream is rotting away
item.description: As one of Dayton’s former guardians, Schmidt fears less instability than a quiet collapse of trust, as youth reject segregated schools, politicians glorify war criminals, and Europe fails to turn Bosnia’s pro-EU mood into real opportunities.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Berechenbare Risiken – unberechenbare Politik? Warum Deutschland jetzt aus Worten Gesetze machen muss
item.description: Mit berechenbaren Risiken kann die forschende Pharmaindustrie umgehen - mit politischer Unberechenbarkeit nicht. Warum eine Standortklausel nun ein erster Schritt in Richtung Verlässlichkeit am Standort Deutschland sein kann.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Revealed: The chancellor’s plan to survive the budget
item.description: With the budget barely a fortnight away, Chancellor John Healey is warning of mounting economic headwinds. Can he ease the pressure on the public finances without loosening the purse strings? Sam Coates and Anne McElvoy test the tightrope Healey is attempting to walk ahead of a major speech to the International Monetary Fund. Elsewhere, is […]

item.title: [EU Observer] EU’s 2026 rule‑of‑law report doesn’t trigger real action, says human rights watchdog
item.description: The EU's picture of rule-of-law improvements is rosy, but civil liberties groups were not fooled. A new analysis reveals the commission's recommendations to have been adopted 4 times out of 100, while most remain ignored.

item.title: [Politico Europe] The EU budget battle just got nastier
item.description: Germany has rejected Ireland’s proposal for the EU’s next seven-year budget, despite €159 billion in cuts. And it’s not alone: Governments are divided over where the cuts should fall, while the European Parliament is threatening to block the deal. Zoya Sheftalovich and Nick Vinocur unpack the backlash and what it means for this week’s EU […]

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump’s midterm peril
item.description: Losing the Republican majority in the chamber would be bruising for the president. A vote in rural Iowa may determine his fate

item.title: [Financial Times] Wall Street’s record-breaking trading streak set to cool
item.description: Analysts forecast sharp slowdown when banks report third-quarter results next week after a bumper start to the year

item.title: [Financial Times] There is a smarter way to tax the rich
item.description: Increasing US corporate tax raises government revenues without harming the tax base

item.title: [Financial Times] ‘Worrying omens’ stalk global economy despite resilient growth
item.description: Research for the FT shows major economies are withstanding the Iran shock but concerns about rising public debt will loom over IMF and World Bank meetings

item.title: [Financial Times] Nato should prepare for deadly Russian ‘hybrid’ attack, says Poland
item.description: Foreign minister Radosław Sikorski says risk of casualties is rising as Moscow escalates sabotage campaign on European soil

item.title: [Financial Times] The huge lurking leverage of AI hyperscalers
item.description: While equity investors look to sunny futures, creditors are scrutinising liabilities like leases on data centres

item.title: [EU Observer] This WEEK: Leaders to focus on economy at EU summit, in shadow of Russia threat and Middle East turmoil
item.description: The EU summit dominates the agenda this week, as 27 heads of state and government gather in Brussels for a two-day meeting.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Wie Trumps Ölkrise zur Ukraine-Frage wird
item.description: Donald Trump verkündet eine „Energie-Waffenruhe“ zwischen der Ukraine und Russland an. Fraglich allerdings ist, was die beiden Länder davon wirklich wissen. Um den heimischen Druck durch steigende Ölpreise abzufedern, lockert Trump zuvor die Sanktionen gegen Russland. Weil er dafür von Wolodymyr Selenskyj kritisiert wird, fordert er, die Ukraine brauche einen neuen Präsidenten. Währenddessen ringen die […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] How can Europe leverage laws to secure cloud sovereignty?
item.description: Europe doesn’t have to choose between acting fast and building a solid foundation for sovereignty.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU lacks influence(rs): No content creators at leaders’ summit
item.description: The Council wanted social media stars to cover its meetings, but EU countries failed to pick any for this week's big meeting.

item.title: [DW] Schools crisis in France: Investment fails to inspire confidence
item.description: For weeks, schoolchildren in France have been protesting the failing education system. Compared to many other countries, France invests heavily in education but critics say that the funds are not distributed fairly.

item.title: [DW] Macron and Steinmeier struggle to revive Franco-German ties
item.description: Presidents Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Emmanuel Macron are about to step down from their offices. Their meeting in France made it clear how urgently the Franco-German partnership needs new momentum.

item.title: [DW] Poland: Lifeline for Ukrainian refugees confronts donor fatigue and online abuse as anti-Ukrainian sentiment grows
item.description: A Ukrainian woman who fled the war in her country built a lifeline for refugees in Poland. Now her organization faces donor fatigue, funding cuts and rising hostility as support for Ukrainians in Poland wanes.

item.title: [DW] Bosnia-Herzegovina will soon have a new grand mufti
item.description: The new leader of the Islamic Community in Bosnia-Herzegovina will be elected on October 10. The reis-ul-ulema's role is not only important for Muslims in the country itself, but could inspire Muslims across Europe.

item.title: [DW] Finland, the world's happiest nation, faces a glum winter
item.description: Finns have many reasons to feel content, but the country's pile of debt is not one of them. Russia's war in Ukraine has added to the fiscal burden. Can the Nordic nation absorb another shock?

item.title: [EU Observer] EU trade chief hails ‘crucial first step’ as Beijing talks avoid trade war
item.description: Concessions on electric cars, rare earths and tariffs should be enough for EU and Chinese officials to be able to claim success from trade talks which ended on Friday.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘When you laugh at a dictator, you take away his power’: Artist behind viral naked Trump statue speaks out
item.description: Inspired by Hans Christian Andersen's fairytale, a gold-covered statue of a naked Trump in the halls of European Parliament is meant to make politicians think about democracy, says 'Orange Plague' artist Jens Galschiøt.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU puts 46 more mines and recycling plants on ‘strategic’ list, without closing funding gap
item.description: The EU added 46 strategic minerals projects on Friday, saying progress so far has been ‘very tangible’, but its own figures show little fresh EU financing has materialised.

item.title: [EU Observer] Nato state Montenegro detains top Russian war-blogger Rybar, on suspicion of plotting hybrid tricks (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,688)
item.description: While Rybar’s pro-war editors complain of tightening fronts near Sloviansk, Komar and Dobropillia, independent maps and Ukrainian sources show Moscow’s forces clawing back exaggerated gains as Kyiv tests ambitious advances on the ground and in Russia’s digital backbone.

item.title: [EU Observer] Agrochemical lobbyists are defending a toxic model of agriculture that is heading for collapse
item.description: As pesticide lobbyists dominate a key hearing in Strasbourg, the EU risks locking farmers and citizens into a costly, chemical-dependent food system that poisons water, fuels disease and drains billions in EU subsidies away from real sustainable farming.
